replacements.old:
**The labels come from the scene description, never from pixels.** The renderer takes a list of `SceneObject`s and draws them, so the answer to every question is a function of that
list. If you wanted to know what the right answer is, you would never look at the image; if the model gets it right, it must have extracted the information from the image. That is
what makes this a clean testbed.
replacements.new: **The labels come from the scene description, never from pixels.** The renderer takes a list of `SceneObject`s and draws them; the correct answer is an exact function of that list. An individual correct model answer can still come from a prior or a lucky guess. Evidence that the model uses the image comes from comparing matched image interventions and the text-only, image-only, blank, noise and shuffled-image controls below. Exact scene labels let us score those comparisons without inferring ground truth from model behavior.

rationale: GV-06: distinguish exact ground truth from evidence for image use; individual correctness does not establish causality.
